children: , the aerospace and defense giant, landed a $729 million commitment from Sweden for roughly ten HIMARS systems as its shares traded at $525.28 Monday. The package covers ammunition, deliveries beginning in 2027 and Swedish production through a partnership between Saab and Lockheed. This is more than another weapons orderit pulls a new NATO customer deeper into the company's missile ecosystem.

Washington previously approved a potential $930 million sale covering 20 launchers and a wider selection of weapons. Sweden's final agreement is approximately 21.6% smaller, but investors should not mistake that gap for a discount. The scope changed sharply, with the eventual purchase including roughly half the number of launchers.

Lockheed's Missiles and Fire Control division produced $4.10 billion of second-quarter sales, surging 19% with a 14.5% operating margin. Sweden's order equals nearly 17.8% of one quarter's segment revenue, although the money will flow in gradually as production and deliveries advance. At $525.28, the stock also sits 6.51% below its $561.86 GF Value estimatea modest valuation gap backed by another long-cycle contract feeding Lockheed's already busy missile factories.

title: Lockheed's $729 Million HIMARS Win Feeds a 19% Missile-Sales Surge
